The pooled gene-expression (log2(TPM+1)) distribution across all cell lines is RIGHT-SKEWED (positively skewed).

Numeric result: scipy.stats.skew (Fisher-Pearson moment coefficient) = 0.6897 (≈0.69) on the pooled vector of 32,017,874 values (19,138 protein-coding genes × 1,673 cell lines).

Interpretation: A positive skewness of ~0.69 indicates a right-skewed distribution — most expression values cluster at low-to-moderate log2(TPM+1) values with a long right tail of highly expressed genes. This is confirmed by supporting checks: mean (2.612) > median (2.342), and the upper tail stretches far beyond the lower (P99 = 9.23 vs P1 = -0.038; right-tail spread P99–P50 = 6.88 vs left-tail spread P50–P1 = 2.38).

Per approved defaults: all 19,138 genes included (no filtering), no imputation (no NaN/zero present), and the ~3.5M slightly-negative batch-corrected values were retained (no clipping).
